marks.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי: סוחרי כסות ... חייבין חטאת, ולא סוחרי כסות בלבד אמרו אלא כל אדם
R' Yochanan: one who goes out on Shabbat with a folded cloak lying on his shoulder is liable to a sin-offering
כי הא דרב שישא בריה דרב אידי מתנאה בסדינו הוה -- as Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi, who adorned himself with his sheet
R' Zeira, of the first [fold] R' Yirmeya showed him: forbidden
Rav Huna: one who shakes his cloak on Shabbat is liable to a sin-offering
Ulla, seeing the Rabbis of Pumbedita shake their cloaks: the Rabbis are desecrating Shabbat
Rav Yosef, to Abaye who hesitated to hand him his hat because there was dew on it: shake [it] and throw [it]
the baraita: a shopkeeper who goes out with coins bound in his sheet is liable to a sin-offering -- and not a shopkeeper alone but every person
R' Yehuda: Hyrcanus son of R' Eliezer ben Hyrcanus went out on Shabbat with a scarf on his shoulder, but with a thread wound on his finger
R' Elai: it is forbidden to make a marzev on Shabbat
once Rebbi went out to the field with both sides of his cloak lying on his shoulder
Ravin: it was not Yehoshua ben Zeiruz but Yehoshua ben Kefusai, R' Akiva's son-in-law
one who bathed in cave water or Tiberias water and dried himself, even with ten towels, may not bring them in his hand
one may smear [oil] and rub gently
the mishna says 'one who bathes' (after the fact), not 'one may bathe' -- so ab initio, no
the mishna teaches cave water alongside Tiberias water: as Tiberias water is hot, so the cave water is hot
